summary: Process switch `owner_gates` lets a Delivery batch the owner's decisions into two fixed gates without deciding anything by default. `per_step`, the default, keeps asking each question when it comes up and every compiler output. At `two_fixed_gates`, gate A presents the scope, the execution plan, every Operation or Governance change it needs, the decision log and the queued questions, and its approval authorizes the plan's writes through Item start; gate B presents the Delivery Review, its follow-ups, the decision log since gate A and the merge. Between the gates a question is queued as a `pending` row of the Delivery's `User Decisions` table, only the tasks that depend on it wait, and the queue is asked as an early gate once every remaining task depends on it. The Software Architect's unchanged escalation clause and the classes in `skill-content/deliver/data/owner-decision-classes.json` are asked at once, and `tools/validate.py` rejects an empty or duplicate class and a clause its agent file no longer states. `delivery_compile.py init` writes the table's header and `check` validates it whenever the section holds it, whatever policy is in force later: unique `D-` ids, a known class, at least two options with the recommendation among them, a `pending` or `answered` status, an answer on every `answered` row and on no `pending` one, `blocks` naming the Delivery's Items by Story id, and `wait_minutes` on an `answered` row that blocked an Item. The gates hold the run to the log: `approve-scope`, `approve-review` and `delivery_git.py publish-delivery-review` refuse while a row is `pending`, `check-plan` lists the pending rows under `pending_decisions`, and `claim-items`, `start-item`, `resume-item` and `reopen-item` refuse an Item a `pending` row blocks with the new finding code `DELIVERY_DECISION_PENDING`. Between the gates, from the Delivery's first execution approval until `approve-review`, `operation_compile.py approve`, `delivery_governance.py approve` and `approve-execution` refuse until an `answered` row names the document they change. Gate A approves the Governance change and applies it before the reservation, which needs the Fence to carry it, and the Operation revisions after it, so a refused reservation leaves only the applied Governance change, as a project document. The host contracts group gate questions in calls of at most four on Claude Code and at most three on Codex, the most `AskUserQuestion` and `request_user_input` take per call, recommended option first. The switch declares `reference_scope: owning_flows`, so its instructions and decision classes reach every task of its owning flows at `two_fixed_gates`: the `/delivery-plan`, `/execution-plan` and `/configure` roles, Operation and Governance steps included, as well as `/deliver`.
